sentences.text: The only known specimen of Nyana rooiwalensis consists of a partial articulated skull and fragmentary skeleton belonging to a juvenile that was three years old at death.
Its generic name Nyana translates as “son” or “child” in Xhosa and “small” in Sesotho.
The specific epithet rooiwalensis denotes the Rooiwal locality where the fossil was recovered.
The holotype skull preserves the braincase, palate, hyoid apparatus and scleral rings, representing the first near-complete sauropodomorph skull from the lower Elliot Formation.
Fossil material of Nyana was uncovered in 2018 within lower Elliot Formation outcrops of the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.
The holotype specimen, catalogued as BP/1/8468, is curated at the Evolutionary Studies Institute.
Nyana is recorded from a single fossil occurrence in the Paleobiology Database.
Body-mass estimates indicate that Nyana weighed about 400 kilograms.
Nyana is placed within the massopodan clade of sauropodomorph dinosaurs.
It belongs to the broader group Sauropodomorpha, itself a subset of the Saurischia class.
Nyana rooiwalensis lived during the Late Triassic Norian–Rhaetian ages in South Africa’s Elliot Formation.
